subject.title: [Feature]: Subagent session reuse for expert agents (avoid new session per spawn)

question: What permanent contract should native `sessions_spawn` use for reusable expert subagent sessions on channels without thread-bound session mode?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the implementation shape controls history isolation, concurrency, routing, cleanup, and plugin/channel API boundaries, so automation should not choose the product semantics.

options.title: Design core native reuse
options.body: Add an explicit core reuse contract with scoped session identity, TTL/liveness checks, locking, cleanup, and docs/tests across native subagent paths.

options.title: Route through non-thread sessions
options.body: Use the broader non-thread persistent-session direction tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53548 and make this issue a native reuse slice of that product work.

options.title: Limit to Teams binding
options.body: Add a Teams-specific binding path, accepting that it would not solve reuse for other non-thread channels and may need migration away from deprecated hook semantics.

recommendation.title: Design core native reuse
recommendation.body: Add an explicit core reuse contract with scoped session identity, TTL/liveness checks, locking, cleanup, and docs/tests across native subagent paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the central subagent spawn and session/tool contract surfaces.
